<!--
Sections in order. Summary, Why, What, How and Test plan are expected on every
pull request; Evidence and References are optional.

A one-line change can have one-line sections. A design decision cannot — the
reasoning is the part that is hard to reconstruct in six months and the part
that stops a settled question being reopened.

Before you open this: `pnpm verify` passes, and nothing below contains a real
name, amount, payee, account or institution. This repository is public and the
subject is a personal ledger.
-->

## Summary

<!-- One or two sentences. What changed, and what is now true that was not
     before. Write it for someone deciding whether to read the rest. -->

## Why

<!-- Why this needs to exist at all. The problem, who or what it hurts, and
     what happens if it is left alone. If it came from an issue or a review
     finding, say which. -->

## What

<!-- What is actually being fixed or added, stated concretely. If a stated
     guarantee was false, quote it. If a figure was wrong, give both values. -->

## How

<!-- The approach, and — importantly — what else was considered and rejected.
     If enforcement moved to a new layer (constraint, trigger, role privilege,
     type, registry validation), say which layer and why that one. -->

## Test plan

<!-- How you know it works, in steps someone else could repeat.

     "A gate never seen to fail is not a gate" — if this adds a check, say how
     you made it fail on purpose. Verification by execution counts; verification
     by reading does not, and has missed things here before.

     - [ ] `pnpm verify`
     - [ ] migrations apply cleanly to an empty database
     - [ ] ... -->

## Evidence

<!-- Optional. Command output, before/after figures, query results, timings,
     screenshots. Redact first. -->

## References

<!-- Optional. Issues, `SPEC.md` sections, defect IDs, prior pull requests. -->
